sentences.en: This is Hidden Brain.
sentences.zh: 这里是《隐藏的大脑》。

sentences.en: I'm Shankar Vedantam.
sentences.zh: 我是尚卡尔·韦丹塔姆。

sentences.en: The television series Never Have I Ever is a coming-of-age story about the ups and downs of high school.
sentences.zh: 电视剧《好想做一次》是一部关于高中生活起伏的成长故事。

sentences.en: There's popular kids, unpopular kids, and drama.
sentences.zh: 里面有受欢迎的孩子、不受欢迎的孩子，还有各种抓马。

sentences.en: There are lots and lots of crushes.
sentences.zh: 有数不清的暗恋。

sentences.en: And of course, there's applying for college.
sentences.zh: 当然，还有申请大学。

sentences.en: One of the show's main characters is an overachiever.
sentences.zh: 剧中的主要角色之一是个超级学霸。

sentences.en: Ben is determined to get into his dream school, Columbia University.
sentences.zh: 本决心考入他梦想中的学校——哥伦比亚大学。

sentences.en: His schedule is packed with studying, extracurriculars, and tests.
sentences.zh: 他的日程表排得满满当当，全都是学习、课外活动和考试。

sentences.en: Ben has no time for friends, socializing, or even breakfaSt.
sentences.zh: 本根本没有时间陪朋友、社交，甚至连吃早餐的时间都没有。

sentences.en: Time for breakfast, my little prince.
sentences.zh: 该吃早饭了，我的小王子。

sentences.en: No time, Patty.
sentences.zh: 没时间，帕蒂。

sentences.en: I'll just eat a jerky stick on the way.
sentences.zh: 我在路上随便啃根肉干就行。

sentences.en: At school, Ben's time-starved schedule elicits eye rolls from his classmates.
sentences.zh: 在学校里，本这种极度缺乏时间的日程安排引来同学们的一阵白眼。

sentences.en: I have some free time between 1.15 and 2 a.m.
sentences.zh: 今晚一点十五分到两点之间

sentences.en: tonight to work on this.
sentences.zh: 我有一点空闲时间来处理这个。

sentences.en: Are you out of your mind?
sentences.zh: 你疯了吗？

sentences.en: We're not operating on your psycho schedule.
sentences.zh: 我们可不按你那发疯的日程来。

sentences.en: Both of you guys just come to my house after school.
sentences.zh: 你们俩放学后直接来我家吧。

sentences.en: I can't.
sentences.zh: 我不能去。

sentences.en: That's when I Zoom with my Mandarin teacher.
sentences.zh: 那会儿我要跟我的普通话老师上Zoom网课。

sentences.en: Even Ben's principal has become concerned about his constant battle with time.
sentences.zh: 甚至连本的校长也开始担心他与时间的持久战。

sentences.en: Your schedule is untenable.
sentences.zh: 你的日程安排简直荒谬。

sentences.en: You don't even have a lunch period anymore.
sentences.zh: 你现在连午休时间都没有了。

sentences.en: I don't need a lunch period.
sentences.zh: 我不需要午休时间。

sentences.en: Mm-hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯哼。

sentences.en: Yes, I've seen you with your meat sticks.
sentences.zh: 对，我见过你啃肉条的样子。

sentences.en: Eventually, the stress lands Ben in the hospital.
sentences.zh: 最终，巨大的压力把本送进了医院。

sentences.en: While Ben's character is exaggerated for comic effect, many people, including those who graduated high school years ago, can relate.
sentences.zh: 虽然剧中本的形象为了喜剧效果有所夸张，但许多人，包括那些多年前就高中毕业的人，都能感同身受。

sentences.en: Lofty goals, demanding jobs, and the pressures of parenthood leave many of us feeling burned out, on edge, and overwhelmed.
sentences.zh: 崇高的目标、苛刻的工作以及为人父母的压力，让我们许多人感到筋疲力尽、焦躁不安、不堪重负。

sentences.en: This week on Hidden Brain, how the solution to not having enough time might require us to rethink our relationship with time.
sentences.zh: 本周《隐藏的大脑》将探讨：解决时间不够用的问题，可能需要我们重新审视自己与时间的关系。

sentences.en: When we're thinking about this resource, it makes us spend more deliberately in ways that are aligned with our values, in ways that make us feel happier.
sentences.zh: 当我们思考这种资源时，它能促使我们更深思熟虑地进行消费，使其符合我们的价值观，从而让我们感到更快乐。

sentences.en: Most of us live our lives in a blur.
sentences.zh: 我们大多数人的生活都在一片模糊中度过。

sentences.en: We speed through our days, rush to drop off kids, battle work deadlines, squeeze in emails before bed.
sentences.zh: 我们争分夺秒地度过每一天，急匆匆地送孩子上学，应付工作截止日期，在睡觉前还要见缝插针地回邮件。

sentences.en: Lots of us dream of doing less, much less.
sentences.zh: 我们许多人都梦想着少做一点，再少做一点。

sentences.en: We fantasize about striking it rich and quitting our jobs.
sentences.zh: 我们幻想着一夜暴富然后辞职不干。

sentences.en: At UCLA, Cassie McGillner Holmes studies the relationship between time and well-being.
sentences.zh: 在加州大学洛杉矶分校，卡茜·麦吉尔纳·霍姆斯专门研究时间和幸福感之间的关系。

sentences.en: Among other things, she has studied what happens to people who get their wish to have all the time in the world.
sentences.zh: 除此以外，她还研究过那些如愿以偿获得全世界所有时间的人身上会发生什么。

sentences.en: Cassie Holmes, welcome to Hidden Brain.
sentences.zh: 卡茜·霍姆斯，欢迎来到《隐藏的大脑》。

sentences.en: Hi, Shankar.
sentences.zh: 嗨，尚卡尔。

sentences.en: Thank you so much for having me.
sentences.zh: 非常感谢邀请我来。

sentences.en: This is so exciting.
sentences.zh: 这太令人兴奋了。

sentences.en: Cassie, I'd like to take you back to a point in your life when you had just had a baby, your maternity leave had ended, and you were on your first work trip to New York.
sentences.zh: 卡茜，我想带你回到你人生中的某个时间点，当时你刚生完孩子，产假已经结束，你正踏上前往纽约的第一次工作差旅。

sentences.en: Can you paint me a picture of what your life felt like at the time?
sentences.zh: 你能给我描绘一下当时你的生活感受吗？

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 可以的。

sentences.en: My life felt crazy at the time.
sentences.zh: 当时我的生活简直疯狂极了。

sentences.en: And so, yeah, when my son was four months old, I was invited to give a talk at Columbia's Business School up in New York, and I said yes.
sentences.zh: 所以，嗯，当我的儿子四个月大时，我应邀去纽约的哥伦比亚商学院做一个讲座，我答应了。

sentences.en: And it was a crazy day, but not unlike other crazy days.
sentences.zh: 那是个疯狂的日子，但也和其他疯狂的日子没什么两样。

sentences.en: It's just I remember it quite vividly.
sentences.zh: 只是我对那一天的记忆依然相当鲜明。

sentences.en: I woke up early, traveled up to New York to give my presentation, which was followed by back-to-back meetings and then sort of colleague dinner.
sentences.zh: 我起得很早，赶往纽约进行演讲，接着是一个接一个的会议，然后是某种同事晚宴。

sentences.en: And I rushed out of the dinner trying to make the very last train that would get me home to my son and my husband back in Philadelphia.
sentences.zh: 我从晚宴上匆忙赶出来，想要赶上最后一班火车，好回到费城的家去见我的儿子和丈夫。

sentences.en: And the cab driver, as you know, New York cab drivers are already driving very fast and too faSt.
sentences.zh: 出租车司机——你知道的，纽约的出租车司机本来就开得非常快，甚至太快了。

sentences.en: But I was yelling at him, which I don't tend to yell.
sentences.zh: 但我当时在对大喊大叫，我平时其实不怎么大喊大叫的。

sentences.en: I was like, can you please hurry up to get me to this train?
sentences.zh: 我当时就说，你能开快点把我送到这趟火车上吗？

sentences.en: I cannot miss it.
sentences.zh: 我绝对不能错过它。

sentences.en: And I didn't miss the train.
sentences.zh: 我没有错过那辆火车。

sentences.en: But when I was sitting on the train that night, I remember looking out the window.
sentences.zh: 但那天晚上坐在火车上时，我记得我望向窗外。

sentences.en: And as the sort of darkness was whizzing by and everyone was asleep in their homes and just like I should have been asleep in my home and my husband and baby were asleep in our home.
sentences.zh: 当黑暗飞驰而过，每个人的家都沉浸在睡梦中，就像我本来也应该在自己的家里睡觉一样，我的丈夫和宝宝也在我们家里熟睡。

sentences.en: And I was realizing just how fast everything was going by and it was such a blur between the pressures of being an assistant professor.
sentences.zh: 我当时意识到一切都过得太快了，在身为助理教授的种种压力之间，这一切都成了一片模糊。

sentences.en: So, you know, work, the pressure or wanting to be a good parent, a good partner, a good friend, you know, with the never ending pile of chores that were waiting me at home.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道的，工作，想要成为好父母、好伴侣、好朋友的压力，还有你知道的，家里永远做不完的家务活。

sentences.en: It all felt like too much.
sentences.zh: 这一切都让人觉得难以承受。

sentences.en: There was just simply sort of too much to do.
sentences.zh: 简直就是有太多事情要做。

sentences.en: And I remember wondering, I was like, not only do I not have enough time to sort of do it all, I wasn't feeling like I could do it all well or enjoy any of it along the way.
sentences.zh: 我记得当时我在想，不仅我没有足够的时间把所有事情都做好，而且我也不觉得自已能把每件事都做好，或者在过程中享受其中的任何一部分。

sentences.en: So sometime later, Cassie, you finally get to take a break.
sentences.zh: 那么过了一段时间后，卡茜，你终于有机会休息一下了。

sentences.en: I understand you took a trip to Mexico.
sentences.zh: 据我了解，你去了墨西哥旅行。

sentences.en: How did it go?
sentences.zh: 进展得怎么样？

sentences.en: Well, it was a trip to Mexico that I was so excited about because, you know, it continued to be on the heels of crazy days of, you know,
sentences.zh: 嗯，我对那次墨西哥之行感到非常兴奋，因为，你知道的，在那之前刚刚经历了一连串疯狂的日子，你知道的，

sentences.en: the busyness of work and getting the kids ready and teaching and all that sort of stuff.
sentences.zh: 工作繁忙、给孩子准备东西、上课以及诸如此类的事情。

sentences.en: And so I was so excited about the idea of just sitting on the beach with the book with nothing to do.
sentences.zh: 所以我一想到能在海滩上安安静静地看书、什么也不用做，就感到兴奋不已。

sentences.en: And that sounded more than delightful.
sentences.zh: 听起来简直不能再美妙了。

sentences.en: And it was delightful until the morning of the fourth day.
sentences.zh: 而且它确实很美妙，直到第四天早晨。

sentences.en: And I woke up and I was like, you know, tapping on my husband's shoulder.
sentences.zh: 我醒来后，你知道的，轻轻拍了拍我丈夫的肩膀。

sentences.en: I'm like, all right, so what are we going to do today?
sentences.zh: 我说，好了，那我们今天要干什么呢？

sentences.en: I was done doing nothing.
sentences.zh: 我已经受够无所事事了。

sentences.en: And I was eager to get going again.
sentences.zh: 我渴望重新行动起来。

sentences.en: For many of us, this is a relatable experience.
sentences.zh: 对我们许多人来说，这是一种感同身受的经历。

sentences.en: We look forward to going on vacation only to feel bored or antsy after a few days.
sentences.zh: 我们期盼着去度假，结果却在几天后感到无聊或烦躁不安。

sentences.en: Just like Cassie, we are unhappy when we are busy and we are unhappy when we have too much time on our hands.
sentences.zh: 就像卡茜一样，我们忙碌时会不开心，而手头有太多空闲时间时同样不开心。

sentences.en: Cassie and her colleagues, Marissa Sharif and Hal Hirshfield, have studied the connection between having free time, or discretionary time, as Cassie puts it,
sentences.zh: 卡茜和她的同事玛丽莎·谢里夫以及哈尔·赫什菲尔德研究了拥有空闲时间（用卡茜的话说，即可支配时间）之间的联系，

sentences.en: and people's happiness.
sentences.zh: 以及人们的幸福感。

sentences.en: What we found was interesting.
sentences.zh: 我们的发现很有趣。

sentences.en: The pattern of results showed an upside down U-shape.
sentences.zh: 结果呈现出一个倒U型的曲线模式。

sentences.en: So what that suggests is that on one end, people with too little time were unhappy.
sentences.zh: 这表明，在其中一端，时间太少的人并不快乐。

sentences.en: So that was, you know, me on the train that night.
sentences.zh: 所以那就是，你知道的，那天晚上在火车上的我。

sentences.en: But what was surprising to us was the other side of that arc, right?
sentences.zh: 但让我们感到惊讶的是这条弧线的另一端，对吧？

sentences.en: And what we found was that beyond a certain amount, there was such thing as having too much time.
sentences.zh: 我们发现，超过一定限度后，确实存在“拥有太多时间”这回事。

sentences.en: So when people had a whole, whole lot of discretionary hours in the day, they were also dissatisfied.
sentences.zh: 因此，当人们一天中有大量大量的可支配时间时，他们同样会感到不满意。

sentences.en: So it's almost a paradox, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 所以这几乎是一个悖论，不是吗？

sentences.en: Because very busy people imagine that, you know, they dream about the day they can just put up their feet and do nothing.
sentences.zh: 因为非常忙碌的人会想象，你知道的，他们梦想着有一天能把脚翘起来什么都不做。

sentences.en: And, of course, when that day actually arrives, very quickly, like you found, you found yourself frustrated.
sentences.zh: 当然，当那一天真的到来时，很快地，就像你所发现的那样，你会发现自己感到沮丧。

sentences.en: And this is, it's apparently not just you, it's a widespread phenomenon.
sentences.zh: 而且这显然不仅仅发生在你身上，这是一个普遍存在的现象。

sentences.en: What explains the paradox?
sentences.zh: 是什么解释了这个悖论？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And what our data suggests is that when people have too many discretionary hours in a day, they feel unproductive.
sentences.zh: 我们的数据表明，当人们一天中有太多可支配时间时，他们会觉得自己毫无成效。

sentences.en: And from that, it undermines their sense of purpose.
sentences.zh: 由此一来，这就削弱了他们的目标感。

sentences.en: And with that, people are dissatisfied.
sentences.zh: 随之而来的便是人们的不满。

sentences.en: You know, a few years back, there was a study in the United Kingdom that looked at the cognitive function of thousands of retirees.
sentences.zh: 你知道，几年前，英国曾做过一项研究，调查了数千名退休人员的认知功能。

sentences.en: These were people who had held a variety of different jobs at different salary levels.
sentences.zh: 这些人曾从事过各种薪资水平不同的不同工作。

sentences.en: And the researchers gave people a cognitive memory test 14 years before they retired and then 14 years after they retired.
sentences.zh: 研究人员在这些人退休前14年以及退休后14年分别对他们进行了认知记忆测试。

sentences.en: Can you tell me what they found, Cassie?
sentences.zh: 卡茜，你能告诉我他们发现了什么吗？

sentences.en: So what they found was that people's cognitive functioning decreased dramatically following retirement in terms of their verbal memory.
sentences.zh: 他们发现，退休后，人们在言语记忆方面的认知功能急剧下降。

sentences.en: And this is interesting because it suggests that when people have too much discretionary time on their hands, that it's less sort of cognitively engaging and stimulating.
sentences.zh: 这很有趣，因为它表明当人们手头有太多可支配时间时，这在认知上的投入和刺激就会减少。

sentences.en: And so what this is all pointing to, I think, is that work for many is a source of feeling engaged, feeling productive.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为这一切所指向的是，对许多人来说，工作是获得投入感和成就感的源泉。

sentences.en: With the retiree study, it is cognitive stimulation, mental stimulation.
sentences.zh: 在退休人员研究中，这就是认知刺激、精神刺激。

sentences.en: And without that, we're not only bored, but we feel less purpose.
sentences.zh: 如果没有这些，我们不仅会感到无聊，还会觉得目标感减少。

sentences.en: We are less engaged and with that, less satisfied.
sentences.zh: 我们的投入度降低，随之而来的满足感也减少了。

sentences.en: Many of us live busy lives.
sentences.zh: 我们许多人都过着忙碌的生活。

sentences.en: We rush to work, check our email, ferry kids around.
sentences.zh: 我们赶着上班、查邮件、接送孩子。

sentences.en: We feel our time is stretched thin, and we fantasize about the day when we can finally do nothing.
sentences.zh: 我们觉得时间被压缩得很紧，并幻想着有一天我们终于可以什么都不做。

sentences.en: When that day comes, however, we often find ourselves confronting the opposite problem.
sentences.zh: 然而，当那一天到来时，我们往往发现自己面临着相反的问题。

sentences.en: We are bored, hungry for meaning and purpose.
sentences.zh: 我们感到无聊，渴望意义和目标。

sentences.en: Being too idle, like being too busy, seems to make us unhappy.
sentences.zh: 无所事事就像过于忙碌一样，似乎都会让我们不快乐。

sentences.en: When we come back, Cassie's research examines how our perceptions of time influence the way we spend it.
sentences.zh: 稍后回来，卡茜的研究将探讨我们对时间的感知如何影响我们花费时间的方式。

sentences.en: You're listening to Hidden Brain.
sentences.zh: 您正在收听的是《隐藏的大脑》。

sentences.en: I'm Shankar Vedantam.
sentences.zh: 我是尚卡尔·韦丹塔姆。

sentences.en: This is Hidden Brain.
sentences.zh: 这里是《隐藏的大脑》。

sentences.en: I'm Shankar Vedantam.
sentences.zh: 我是尚卡尔·韦丹塔姆。

sentences.en: When most of us feel overwhelmed by life and by work, we tend to locate the problem in our circumstances.
sentences.zh: 当大多数人被生活和工作压得喘不过气时，我们往往把问题归咎于我们的处境。

sentences.en: We say, I have too many deadlines staring me in the face.
sentences.zh: 我们会说，摆在我面前的死线实在太多了。

sentences.en: I have too many commitments on my plate.
sentences.zh: 我手头要承担的承诺太多了。

sentences.en: I have no time.
sentences.zh: 我没有时间。

sentences.en: When we think about the solutions to these problems, we often resort to daydreams and fantasy.
sentences.zh: 当我们思考这些问题的解决方案时，往往会求助于白日梦和幻想。

sentences.en: Maybe I'll win the lottery and won't have to work anymore.
sentences.zh: 也许我会中彩票，然后就不用再工作了。

sentences.en: Maybe I could run away to a tropical island where my only responsibility is to sit under a coconut tree and sip margaritas.
sentences.zh: 也许我可以逃到一个热带小岛上，在那里我唯一的责任就是坐在椰子树下啜饮玛格丽特酒。

sentences.en: At UCLA, psychologist Cassie Holmes has come to believe that many people underestimate how much control they do have in making their lives less busy and stressful.
sentences.zh: 在加州大学洛杉矶分校，心理学家卡茜·霍姆斯渐渐相信，许多人低估了自己在让生活不那么忙碌和紧张方面所拥有的掌控力。

sentences.en: A powerful moment of insight in Cassie's life occurred one day in 2017 as she was racing across campus with a preschooler in tow.
sentences.zh: 卡茜人生中一个强有力的顿悟时刻发生在2017年的某一天，当时她正带着一个学龄前儿童在校园里急匆匆地赶路。

sentences.en: I didn't have a long commute.
sentences.zh: 我的通勤时间并不长。

sentences.en: I could walk through beautiful UCLA campus with my three-year-old to take him to preschool and me to work.
sentences.zh: 我可以带着三岁的儿子穿过美丽的加州大学洛杉矶分校校园，把他送到幼儿园，然后我去上班。

sentences.en: And there was one morning in particular where the sun was shining.
sentences.zh: 就在那个特别的早晨，阳光灿烂。

sentences.en: It was a spring day and the birds were chirping and my son was skipping along as happy as could be.
sentences.zh: 那是一个春日，小鸟在歌唱，我的儿子一蹦一跳地开心极了。

sentences.en: And I was charging ahead because I was thinking about the meeting that I was going to be late to and also thinking about all the things that I had to do that day when I dropped him off.
sentences.zh: 而我却在大步流星地往前赶，因为我在想着我要迟到的那个会议，还在想着把他放下后那天我必须要做的一大堆事情。

sentences.en: And I heard him, he was like, Mom, stop.
sentences.zh: 然后我听到他说，妈妈，停下来。

sentences.en: And I was like, we don't have time to stop.
sentences.zh: 而我说，我们没时间停下来。

sentences.en: Hurry up.
sentences.zh: 快点。

sentences.en: And he's like, Mom, please stop.
sentences.zh: 他说，妈妈，请停一下。

sentences.en: And I turn around and I see that his nose is buried in a bush of roses.
sentences.zh: 我转过身去，看到他的鼻子正埋在一丛玫瑰花里。

sentences.en: And I, without thinking, these words came out of my mouth.
sentences.zh: 而我不假思索地，这些话就脱口而出了。

sentences.en: I was like, we don't have time to stop and smell the roses.
sentences.zh: 我说，我们没时间停下来闻闻花香。

sentences.en: And when I heard those words, I did stop.
sentences.zh: 当我听到这些话时，我真的停了下来。

sentences.en: I was like, oh, my gosh.
sentences.zh: 我想，天哪。

sentences.en: I am so in my head.
sentences.zh: 我太沉浸在自己的世界里了。

sentences.en: I am so thinking about what's next that I was oblivious to this perfect scene that I was in that my son was absolutely noticing.
sentences.zh: 我满脑子都在想接下来要做什么，以至于对眼前的这个完美场景视而不见，而我的儿子却实实在在地注意到了它。

sentences.en: And as a time and happiness researcher and expert, yelling into the air that we don't have time to stop and smell the roses was definitely a wake up call.
sentences.zh: 作为一个时间和幸福感的研究人员和专家，冲着空气大喊我们没时间停下来闻闻花香，绝对是一个警钟。

sentences.en: In her lab, Cassie began to ask whether she had defined the problem wrong in her own life.
sentences.zh: 在她的实验室里，卡茜开始反思自己是否在生活中把问题搞错了。

sentences.en: When she thought about being a young working mom and the many pressures on her time at work and at home, it felt really stressful.
sentences.zh: 当她回想自己作为一个年轻的职场妈妈，在工作和家庭中面临着种种时间压力时，确实感到压力山大。

sentences.en: But was the problem a lack of time or the way she was thinking about time?
sentences.zh: 但问题究竟是缺乏时间，还是她对时间的思考方式呢？

sentences.en: She decided to apply the tools of science to her own life and to closely track how she was spending her days.
sentences.zh: 她决定将科学工具应用到自己的生活中，并密切追踪自己是如何度过每一天的。

sentences.en: What time tracking does is that you write down what you're doing every half hour.
sentences.zh: 时间追踪就是把你每半小时在做的事情写下来。

sentences.en: What's the activity you're doing?
sentences.zh: 你正在进行的活动是什么？

sentences.en: And not being so broad like, I'm at work.
sentences.zh: 而且不能太笼统，比如“我在上班”这种。

sentences.en: But in particular, what are you doing at work?
sentences.zh: 但具体来说，你在工作中都在做什么？

sentences.en: What project are you working on?
sentences.zh: 你在进行什么项目？

sentences.en: And not so broad as, oh, it's family time.
sentences.zh: 而且不要太宽泛，比如“哦，这是家庭时间”。

sentences.en: What are you doing during that family time?
sentences.zh: 在那段家庭时间里你具体在做什么？

sentences.en: And it's important to not just write what you're doing, but I also rate on a 10-point scale how happy, how joyful, how satisfying I feel on having spent that time.
sentences.zh: 重要的一点不仅是写下你在做什么，我还会用10分制来评估我花这些时间时的幸福感、快乐感和满足感。

sentences.en: So one can look back and have their own personalized data set that captures how they spent their time and it allows them to pull out what are those activities that tend to produce the greatest amount of happiness for them.
sentences.zh: 这样人们回头看时，就能拥有一套属于自己的个性化数据集，记录他们是如何度过时间的，这能让他们找出那些最容易给自己带来幸福感的活动。

sentences.en: What are those activities that tend to produce the least amount of happiness for them?
sentences.zh: 哪些活动最不容易给他们带来幸福感？

sentences.en: And in addition to that, not just the particular activities, but what are some commonalities across those happiest activities and those least happy activities?
sentences.zh: 除此之外，不仅是具体的活动，这些最快乐的活动和最不快乐的活动之间有什么共同点？

sentences.en: And what this also allows you to do is see just how much time you're spending across these various types of activities.
sentences.zh: 这还能让你清楚地看到自己在这些不同类型的活动上花 了多少时间。

sentences.en: Now, when Cassie talks about choosing activities that produce happiness,
sentences.zh: 现在，当卡西谈到选择能带来幸福的活动时，

sentences.en: it's not like she's saying that our only choices are to do things that make us happy or do things that make us unhappy.
sentences.zh: 这并不是说我们唯一的选择就是在做让人高兴的事或者让人不高兴的事之间二选一。

sentences.en: All of us routinely have to do things that are not fun.
sentences.zh: 我们所有人都得例行公事般地做一些并不好玩的事情。

sentences.en: It's not like we can say, oh, I'm never going to clean my house or do the dishes or go to the dentiSt.
sentences.zh: 我们不能说，哦，我永远不打扫房子、不洗碗、不去看牙医。

sentences.en: What time tracking can show you is that you might not be allocating your time efficiently.
sentences.zh: 时间追踪能向你展示的是，你可能并没有高效分配时间。

sentences.en: Imagine your life was divided into different compartments.
sentences.zh: 想象一下，你的生活被分成了不同的部分。

sentences.en: There are things that you do that are both fun and meaningful, maybe time spent on a stimulating project at work.
sentences.zh: 有些事你既觉得好玩又有意义，比如花时间在工作上做一个有启发性的项目。

sentences.en: Then there's stuff you don't have to do but that you enjoy, like hanging out with friends or going on a vacation.
sentences.zh: 然后还有一些你不用做但你很享受的事，比如和朋友闲逛或去度假。

sentences.en: A third group of activities might be things you have to do even if they are not enjoyable.
sentences.zh: 第三类活动可能是你不得不做的事，即使它们并不让人享受。

sentences.en: Chores fall into this category.
sentences.zh: 家务就属于这一类。

sentences.en: But as Cassie tracked her time, she realized she was spending more time than she needed to on chores.
sentences.zh: 但随着卡西追踪自己的时间，她意识到自己在做家务上花的时间超出了必要程度。

sentences.en: Well, there was a lot of time that I would say was wasted.
sentences.zh: 嗯，有很多时间可以说是被浪费掉了。

sentences.en: And in particular, my source of wasted time is the amount of time I spend on email and responding to my inbox and trying to get through it.
sentences.zh: 具体来说，我浪费时间的来源是我花在电子邮件上、回复收件箱以及试图处理完它们的时间。

sentences.en: Not just in the work day, but also in the evenings.
sentences.zh: 不仅在工作日，还有傍晚。

sentences.en: And so, and looking at my happiness ratings, I was not very happy spending my time on that particular activity.
sentences.zh: 所以，看看我的幸福感评分，我花时间在那项特定的活动上时并不是很高兴。

sentences.en: What I observed in my time tracking data is that I am happiest when I'm spending time one-on-one having that good connecting conversation with the people I love.
sentences.zh: 我在时间追踪数据中观察到的是，当我花时间一对一地与我爱的人进行这种美好的、有联结的对话时，我最快乐。

sentences.en: Whether it is my husband at the end of the week when we have gone out to dinner away from the kitchen cleanup and are not, you know,
sentences.zh: 无论是周末结束时，我和丈夫一起出去吃晚餐，远离厨房的清理工作，并且不是，你知道的，

sentences.en: going through the logistics of parenting in our lives.
sentences.zh: 去处理我们生活中的育儿琐事。

sentences.en: And actually having the conversation that, you know, drew us to each other in the first place.
sentences.zh: 而是进行那种最初把我们吸引到彼此身边、你知道的对话。

sentences.en: When I'm hanging out with my daughter and we are chatting over a cup of coffee for me, hot chocolate for her.
sentences.zh: 当我跟女儿闲逛，我们边喝着咖啡（对我来说）或热巧克力（对她来说）边聊天时。

sentences.en: When I'm having a wonderful sort of enriching conversation with one of my research collaborators,
sentences.zh: 当我与其中一位研究合作者进行某种精彩的、丰富人生的对话时，

sentences.en: walking across the beautiful UCLA's campus to get coffee or my preferred bubble tea, you know, hearing about their lives as well as talking about research.
sentences.zh: 走在美丽的加州大学洛杉矶分校校园里去买咖啡或我最喜欢的珍珠奶茶，你知道的，听他们讲生活中的事，也聊聊研究。

sentences.en: I mean, there's nothing more joyful than that.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，没有什么比这更让人快乐的了。

sentences.en: As Cassie tracked her time like a scientist, she started to see the epiphany she'd had with her preschooler smelling the roses pointed to something much bigger.
sentences.zh: 当卡西像科学家一样追踪她的时间时，她开始发现，她和学龄前儿童闻玫瑰花时获得的顿悟指向了更宏大的东西。

sentences.en: In all sorts of ways, she was not allocating her time to maximize activities that promoted happiness.
sentences.zh: 在各方面，她都没有把时间分配好，以便最大化那些能促进幸福感的活动。

sentences.en: She was allowing things she didn't enjoy, but felt she had to do, to intrude on time set aside for relaxation and rejuvenation.
sentences.zh: 她纵容那些她并不喜欢、但觉得不得不做的事情，去侵占原本留作放松和恢复精力的时间。

sentences.en: She noticed this acutely during a visit to Italy.
sentences.zh: 在一次去意大利的旅行中，她深刻地注意到了这一点。

sentences.en: We went to Tuscany, which was so wonderful.
sentences.zh: 我们去了托斯卡纳，那真是太棒了。

sentences.en: And this was one week that we were carving out to not do work, to not be in that do mode and just be on vacation.
sentences.zh: 这是我们抽出来的一周，不工作，不处于那种“工作”模式，只是纯粹度假。

sentences.en: Yeah, I found myself in the evening looking over, you know, the Tuscan countryside, this beautiful sunset.
sentences.zh: 是的，我发现自己在傍晚时分眺望（你知道的）托斯卡纳的乡村风光、美丽的日落。

sentences.en: And what was going on in my head was planning for what we were going to be doing tomorrow and coordinating that and sort of sneaking onto my phone to try to coordinate when we were going to be picked up to go,
sentences.zh: 而我脑子里想的却是规划我们明天要做什么、协调这些事情，并偷偷摸摸地用手机试图协调我们什么时候被接走去，

sentences.en: you know, to the next little town.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，去下一个小镇。

sentences.en: Even worse than chores intruding on activities that promote happiness, time tracking can show how much time you are spending on things that are neither essential nor joyful.
sentences.zh: 比家务侵占促进幸福的活动更糟糕的是，时间追踪能显示出你在既非必不可少又毫无乐趣的事情上花了多少时间。

sentences.en: Spending time on such activities makes absolutely no sense.
sentences.zh: 把时间花在这样的活动上简直毫无意义。

sentences.en: One of my students, I remember in particular, who, while working towards her degree on the nights and weekends, while working full time, she was so busy.
sentences.zh: 我记得有个学生特别典型，她在全职工作的同时，在晚上和周末攻读学位，忙得不可开交。

sentences.en: Yet when she looked at the data from her week, she realized that she spent a dozen hours on social media.
sentences.zh: 然而，当她查看一周的数据时，她意识到自己竟然在社交媒体上花了十几个小时。

sentences.en: And looking at her ratings, she's like, holy cow, that is so much, particularly given how busy she is.
sentences.zh: 看着她的评分，她觉得：天哪，这太多了，考虑到她那么忙。

sentences.en: And looking at the ratings that she gave, you know, it's like three and four, whereas the activities that she feels too busy that she doesn't have time to do, but gets, you know,
sentences.zh: 再看她给出的评分，你知道的，基本上是三分和四分，而那些她觉得自己忙得没时间做、但在幸福感上能打九分或十分的活动，

sentences.en: a nine or a 10 in terms of happiness, is meeting up with her sister after work for dinner.
sentences.zh: 是下班后和姐姐见面吃晚餐。

sentences.en: And what I think that highlights with respect to the busyness, that we feel too busy to do these things that really matter to us and can really make us feel joyful,
sentences.zh: 我认为这凸显了关于忙碌的一点：我们觉得自己太忙了，没时间做那些对我们真正重要、确实能让我们感到快乐的事情，

sentences.en: that we're too busy to do those, yet so many hours just get mindlessly filled scrolling.
sentences.zh: 我们觉得自己太忙而没空做这些，然而大量的时间却在无意识地刷手机中被消磨掉了。

sentences.en: And it's one of those things on social media that people think, you know, I'm just going to check, it'll just be a couple minutes, but inevitably a couple minutes turns into,
sentences.zh: 社交媒体就是那种人们会觉得“我只是看一眼，就几分钟”的事情，但不可避免地，几分钟会变成，

sentences.en: you know, tens of minutes.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，几十分钟。

sentences.en: But then those tens of minutes over the course of days sum up to hours and hours.
sentences.zh: 然后这几十分钟在好几天的时间里累积起来，就变成了数不清的小时。

sentences.en: And for those of us who feel so time poor, this is important to recognize because it suggests where can we reallocate some of our time so that we can spend more on moments of joy.
sentences.zh: 对于我们这些觉得自己严重缺乏时间的人来说，认识到这一点很重要，因为它暗示了我们可以把哪些时间重新分配，以便把更多时间花在快乐的时刻上。

sentences.en: Cassie also noticed that when she was not mindful about how she spent her time, she would start to multitask.
sentences.zh: 卡西还注意到，当她没有正念地对待自己如何度过时间时，她就会开始多任务处理。

sentences.en: Even when she was doing things that she needed to do and loved to do, her mind would be somewhere else.
sentences.zh: 即使在做她需要做且喜爱做的事情时，她的心思也会飘到别处。

sentences.en: One time, Cassie noticed herself doing this as she was listening to a scientific presentation on the risks of distraction.
sentences.zh: 有一次，卡西注意到自己在听一个关于分心风险的科学演讲时，就在做这种事。

sentences.en: It was just so sort of on the nose.
sentences.zh: 这实在是太贴切了。

sentences.en: As a professor, one of the joys of our work is that we get to go to research seminars where other faculty will come and share the research that we're working on.
sentences.zh: 作为一名教授，我们工作中的乐趣之一就是去参加研究研讨会，其他教职员工会来分享他们正在研究的研究成果。

sentences.en: And it's joyful because we get to learn what is happening in science.
sentences.zh: 这令人快乐，因为我们得以了解科学界正在发生什么。

sentences.en: And there was this fascinating presentation where the researcher was sharing the dangers of being distracted on cell phones among drivers.
sentences.zh: 当时有一个精彩的演讲，研究人员分享了驾驶员在手机上分心的危险。

sentences.en: So being distracted on the cell phone while driving is more deadly, more dangerous than even driving inebriated or drunk.
sentences.zh: 因此，开车时因手机分心比酒后驾车或醉酒驾驶还要致命、还要危险。

sentences.en: And while he was telling us about the dangers of being distracted on our phones, I was distracted.
sentences.zh: 就在他告诉我们分心玩手机的危险时，我分心了。

sentences.en: And on my phone, you know, I was nodding, trying to pretend that I was listening.
sentences.zh: 我一边玩手机，你知道的，一边点头，假装自己在听。

sentences.en: But instead, I was on Amazon going through my to-do list of ordering a gift and wrapping paper for my son to go to a birthday party that week.
sentences.zh: 但实际上我在逛亚马逊，在完成我的待办清单：为儿子当周要去的生日派对订购礼物和包装纸。

sentences.en: And emailing the team, his soccer team, about, you know, who's going to bring the snacks.
sentences.zh: 并且给他的足球队团队发邮件，关于，你知道的，谁来带零食。

sentences.en: So I was being pulled out of this experience that could have been really enriching and illuminating because I was distracted by my to-do liSt.
sentences.zh: 所以我被拉离了本可以非常丰富和启迪心灵的体验，因为我被自己的待办清单分心了。

sentences.en: The less mindful we are about how we deploy our time, the more we feel stressed out and overscheduled.
sentences.zh: 我们对如何安排时间越缺乏正念，我们就越会感到压力山大和日程过载。

sentences.en: This has implications not just for our personal happiness, but how we behave toward others and how others behave toward us.
sentences.zh: 这不仅对我们的个人幸福有影响，还会影响我们对待别人的方式以及别人对待我们的方式。

sentences.en: A famous study in the 1970s demonstrated this.
sentences.zh: 20世纪70年代的一项著名研究证明了这一点。

sentences.en: It's centered around a parable from the Bible, the Good Samaritan who stops to help another person in distress.
sentences.zh: 它围绕着圣经中的一个寓言，即好心的撒玛利亚人停下来帮助另一个陷入困境的人。

sentences.en: This is a really interesting study and conducted among the kindest individuals one could come across, right?
sentences.zh: 这是一项非常有趣的研究，而且是在人们能遇到的最善良的个人当中进行的，对吧？

sentences.en: Some of the participants were told that they were late, that they didn't have a lot of time.
sentences.zh: 一些参与者被告知他们迟到了，他们没有太多时间。

sentences.en: And on their way, there was actually a man on the side who was coughing clearly in need of help.
sentences.zh: 而在他们路过时，路边实际上有一个人正在咳嗽，明显需要帮助。

sentences.en: Unbeknownst to the participants, he was someone who was hired as a confederate for the study.
sentences.zh: 参与者并不知道，这个人是为研究特意雇用的演员。

sentences.en: But what the researchers were looking at is whether someone who was told that they were late, who felt like they were in a hurry, would be likely to stop and help.
sentences.zh: 但研究人员观察的是，那些被告知自己迟到、觉得自己赶时间的人，是否会愿意停下来帮忙。

sentences.en: And indeed, they found when people felt they had scarce time, they were less likely to stop and help someone.
sentences.zh: 果不其然，他们发现当人们觉得自己时间紧迫时，他们就不太可能停下来帮助别人。

sentences.en: I understand that you've conducted a study and found a similar effect.
sentences.zh: 我听说你做过一项研究，也发现了类似的效应。

sentences.en: Is that correct, Cassie?
sentences.zh: 是这样吗，卡西？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Well, I conducted a study among college students, simply leading them to think about how busy or not that they are.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我在大学生中做了一项研究，只是引导他们思考自己有多忙。

sentences.en: And I had them write a paragraph about how busy and how many things they have to do that day versus a control condition where they just wrote about their day.
sentences.zh: 我让他们写一段话，关于他们那天有多忙、有多少事情要做，而对照组则只是写了写他们的一天。

sentences.en: And then I asked them whether they would be willing to stay an extra 15 minutes to help out a high schooler by editing their college application essay.
sentences.zh: 然后我问他们是否愿意多留15分钟，通过帮高中生修改大学申请短文来提供帮助。

sentences.en: And what I found was simply thinking about one's busyness made people less likely to be willing to spend the time to help another.
sentences.zh: 我发现，仅仅是思考自己的忙碌程度，就会让人降低帮助别人的意愿。

sentences.en: Hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯。

sentences.en: So we've looked at lots of ways that the feeling of time scarcity can change our attitudes toward others, change our behavior.
sentences.zh: 所以我们看到了很多现象：时间匮乏感会改变我们对别人的态度，改变我们的行为。

sentences.en: One thing we haven't discussed is how time scarcity in some ways is a trap.
sentences.zh: 有一点我们还没有讨论，那就是时间匮乏在某种程度上是一个陷阱。

sentences.en: It sets us up to make choices that will likely increase our time scarcity in the future.
sentences.zh: 它让我们做出很可能会在未来增加时间匮乏感的选择。

sentences.en: Psychologists described something called the yes, damn effect.
sentences.zh: 心理学家描述了一种叫做“是的-该死”效应的现象。

sentences.en: What is this, Cassie?
sentences.zh: 这是什么，卡西？

sentences.en: Yeah, this is important.
sentences.zh: 对，这很重要。

sentences.en: It's an important study to remember.
sentences.zh: 这是一个需要记住的重要研究。

sentences.en: Gall Zubberman and John Lynch, what they did was they asked people to think about today and all that they have to do today and the busyness of the day.
sentences.zh: 加尔·祖伯曼和约翰·林奇，他们做的是让人们思考今天以及今天要做的一切事情和当天的忙碌程度。

sentences.en: And they also asked them to think about that same day of the month, one month from now.
sentences.zh: 他们还让他们思考一个月后的今天同一天的事情。

sentences.en: And inevitably, people thought that they will have more time available one month from now than they do today.
sentences.zh: 不可避免地，人们会认为一个月后自己能用的时间会比今天多。

sentences.en: But that's absolutely not true because what thinking that you'll have more time available one month from now does is that when you are asked to do things, you say yes.
sentences.zh: 但绝对不是这样的，因为认为一个月后自己有更多可用时间，会直接导致当别人请你帮忙时，你满口答应。

sentences.en: You're like, sure, I will bring the snacks to that event in a month because, you know, like while I'm busy today, I will surely have more time then.
sentences.zh: 你会想：没问题，我一个月后会把零食带到那个活动上，因为，你知道的，虽然我今天很忙，但到时候我肯定有更多时间。

sentences.en: Yes, I will, you know, give a talk for that conference because I will have more time then.
sentences.zh: 是的，我当然会，你知道的，为那个会议做一个演讲，因为我到时候会有更多时间。

sentences.en: But, of course, there's no way I would have time to do that today.
sentences.zh: 但是，当然，我今天绝对没有时间做这个。

sentences.en: And by thinking, having this bias that we think we will have more time available in the future, that we will be less busy in the future than we are today,
sentences.zh: 由于这种偏见，我们认为未来会有更多可用时间，认为未来会比今天不那么忙，

sentences.en: we take on these commitments that when the day comes, that we've said yes.
sentences.zh: 我们接下了这些承诺，而当那一天到来时，我们已经说“好”了。

sentences.en: And then when the day comes, we say damn, hence the yes, damn effect.
sentences.zh: 然后当这一天真的到来时，我们就会说“操”（意为“真该死”），因此得名“是的-该死”效应。

sentences.en: You know, several years ago, I was interviewing Eldar Shafir at Princeton University, and I was telling him how busy I was, how stressed out I was.
sentences.zh: 你知道，几年前，我在普林斯顿大学采访埃尔达·沙菲尔，我告诉他我有多忙，压力有多大。

sentences.en: And he said, let me give you a rule.
sentences.zh: 他说，我给你定个规矩。

sentences.en: If someone suggests you do something two months from now, you should ask yourself, can I do that thing today?
sentences.zh: 如果有人建议你在两个月后做某事，你应该问自己：我今天能做这件事吗？

sentences.en: If it was today, would I be able to do it?
sentences.zh: 如果是在今天，我有能力做吗？

sentences.en: And if the answer to that question is no, you should say no to the thing that's two months from now because presumably you're not going to be any less busy two months from now.
sentences.zh: 如果这个问题的答案是否定的，你应该拒绝那个两个月后的事情，因为可以推测，两个月后你并不会比现在少忙一点。

sentences.en: So I said, okay, that's a great rule.
sentences.zh: 所以我说，好吧，这真是一个好规矩。

sentences.en: I started calling it the Eldar rule.
sentences.zh: 我开始把它叫做“埃尔达规矩”。

sentences.en: But then I asked Eldar, how often do you follow the Eldar rule?
sentences.zh: 但接着我问埃尔达：你多久遵循一次“埃尔达规矩”？

sentences.en: And he said, I never follow it.
sentences.zh: 他说：我从来不遵循。

sentences.en: So it's one thing, Cassie, to know that the bias exists.
sentences.zh: 所以，卡西，知道这种偏见的存在是一回事，

sentences.en: It's another thing to actually do something about it.
sentences.zh: 真正采取行动去解决它是另一回事。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And I would actually sort of put it through a different filter, which it's not only how busy do you think you are today versus will be then,
sentences.zh: 我其实想换一个不同的筛选标准：不仅是对比你觉得今天有多忙和到时候会有多忙，

sentences.en: is, is that task something or that request something that you want to do today, that it seems worthwhile?
sentences.zh: 还要看那项任务或那个请求是不是你今天就想做的事，它看起来是否有价值？

sentences.en: Because it's very easy to say yes to things when you're like, oh, sure, later, because you don't value your time quite so much in the future.
sentences.zh: 因为当你觉得“哦，没问题，以后再说”时，答应别人非常容易，因为你对未来的时间没有那么珍视。

sentences.en: But using a sort of purpose filter or a happiness filter of if I were asked to do this today, would I say no, not just because I'm too busy,
sentences.zh: 但是使用一种目的过滤器或幸福感过滤器——如果今天有人让我做这事，我会拒绝吗？不仅因为我太忙，

sentences.en: but because it's something that I don't want to do and doesn't feel worth my time?
sentences.zh: 而是因为这是我不想做、且觉得不值得花时间的事情？

sentences.en: Mm-hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯哼。

sentences.en: So in other words, we not only discount how busy we're going to be in the future, in some ways we discount the happiness of our future selves by saying,
sentences.zh: 换句话说，我们不仅低估了未来自己会有多忙，在某种程度上，我们还通过这样的话来贬低未来自己的幸福感：

sentences.en: yes, this is not really particularly enjoyable, but I'll just pass that off and my future self will take care of it.
sentences.zh: “是的，这其实不是特别享受，但我先答应下来，以后的我会处理好的。”

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: When we come back, how to recalibrate your relationship with your time?
sentences.zh: 广告回来后，教你如何重新调整你与时间的关系。

sentences.en: You're listening to Hidden Brain.
sentences.zh: 您正在收听的是《隐藏的脑》。

sentences.en: I'm Shankar Vedantam.
sentences.zh: 我是尚卡尔·维丹塔姆。

sentences.en: This is Hidden Brain.
sentences.zh: 这里是《隐藏的脑》。

sentences.en: I'm Shankar Vedantam.
sentences.zh: 我是尚卡尔·维丹塔姆。

sentences.en: Most of us think about time the same way we think about money.
sentences.zh: 我们大多数人看待时间的方式，和看待金钱的方式一样。

sentences.en: We have a limited supply of it, and life would be better if we only had more.
sentences.zh: 我们的供应是有限的，如果能再多一点，生活就会更好。

sentences.en: At UCLA, Cassie Holmes has discovered a number of paradoxes in the way we think about time.
sentences.zh: 在加州大学洛杉矶分校，卡西·霍姆斯发现了我们看待时间的几种悖论。

sentences.en: First, people who have too little to do are often as unhappy as people who have too much.
sentences.zh: 首先，事情太少可做的人，往往和事情太多的人一样不快乐。

sentences.en: Second, when we feel we have no time, it changes our behavior.
sentences.zh: 其次，当我们觉得自己没有时间时，它会改变我们的行为。

sentences.en: It makes us focus less on others.
sentences.zh: 它让我们减少关注他人。

sentences.en: It keeps us from enjoying wonderful things around us.
sentences.zh: 它阻止我们享受身边美好的事物。

sentences.en: It prompts us to make decisions that more or less guarantee we will be overstretched and exhausted in the future.
sentences.zh: 它促使我们做出一些或多或少能保证我们在未来过度透支和精疲力竭的决定。

sentences.en: In her book, Happier Hour, Cassie suggests there is a radically different way to think about time.
sentences.zh: 卡西在她的书《更快乐的一小时》中提出，有一种截然不同的方式来思考时间。

sentences.en: Cassie, you once asked volunteers to think differently about their weekends right before the weekend started.
sentences.zh: 卡西，你曾让志愿者在周末开始前对周末有不同的思考。

sentences.en: What were your instructions to them, and what did you find?
sentences.zh: 你对他们的指令是什么？你发现了什么？

sentences.en: Yes, among a sample of working adults, leading into the weekend, we randomly assigned some to treat that weekend like a vacation.
sentences.zh: 是的，在上班族样本中，在周末即将来临之际，我们随机指定一部分人把那个周末当作假期来对待。

sentences.en: And the others, we told them to treat that weekend like a regular weekend.
sentences.zh: 至于其他人，我们告诉他们把那个周末当作普通的周末来对待。

sentences.en: What did you find?
sentences.zh: 你发现了什么？

sentences.en: We followed up with them on Monday when they returned to work to measure how happy they are.
sentences.zh: 我们在他们周一返回工作岗位时进行了回访，以衡量他们的幸福感。

sentences.en: And what we found was that those who were simply instructed to treat their weekend like a vacation were happier on Monday when they were back at work,
sentences.zh: 我们发现，那些仅仅被指示把周末当作假期来对待的人，在周一返回工作岗位时更加快乐，

sentences.en: and they had enjoyed the weekend more.
sentences.zh: 并且他们更享受那个周末。

sentences.en: And we were interested in what drove this.
sentences.zh: 我们对是什么驱动了这一结果很感兴趣。

sentences.en: Did people spend their time differently?
sentences.zh: 人们花时间的方式不同吗？

sentences.en: And we did find that people, there were slight differences in how people spent their time.
sentences.zh: 我们确实发现人们在如何度过时间上存在微小的差异。

sentences.en: So those who treated the weekend like a vacation did spend a little bit less time doing housework, a little bit less time doing actual work.
sentences.zh: 因此，那些把周末当作假期的人确实少花了一点时间做家务，少花了一点时间做实际工作。

sentences.en: They spent longer eating, so sitting at the dinner table, they spent a little bit more time in bed with their partner.
sentences.zh: 他们花在吃饭上的时间更长了，也就是坐在餐桌旁的时间，他们和伴侣在床上相处的时间也多了一点。

sentences.en: So these are things that are, you know, activities that are like being on vacation.
sentences.zh: 所以这些事情，你知道的，就像是在度假一样的活动。

sentences.en: But it's not like they didn't do any work, and it's not like they didn't do any housework.
sentences.zh: 但这并不是说他们什么工作都没做，也不是说他们没做家务。

sentences.en: What was interesting, too, was that what the activities that they did over the weekend actually didn't significantly influence how they felt when they returned to work on Monday.
sentences.zh: 有趣的是，他们周末进行的活动实际上并没有显著影响他们周一重返工作岗位时的心情。

sentences.en: What did drive that change in happiness was their mindset.
sentences.zh: 真正推动这种幸福感改变的是他们的心态。

sentences.en: So those who were treating the weekend like a vacation were more engaged in the activities they were doing.
sentences.zh: 因此，那些把周末当作假期来过的人，会更投入于他们所做的活动中。

sentences.en: They were more in the present, which allowed them to enjoy that time more, and which then, having enjoyed their weekend more, being fully engaged, not being distracted by,
sentences.zh: 他们更能专注于当下，这让他们更能享受这段时光，进而因为更享受周末、完全投入其中、没有被……分散注意力，

sentences.en: you know, like all of the work or all of the chores that are looming over, you know, waiting for us.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，比如所有那些逼近的工作或琐事，你知道的，都在等着我们。

sentences.en: It allowed them to be happier when they returned to work on Monday.
sentences.zh: 这让他们在周一重返工作岗位时感到更加快乐。

sentences.en: You know, I've often noticed when I travel overseas or to a new city somewhere, you know, you're taking in everything, and you're absorbing everything, and your eyes are wide open.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，我经常发现，当我到海外或某个新城市旅行时，你知道的，你会把一切尽收眼底，你会吸收一切，而且你大开眼界。

sentences.en: But if we look at the people who are the locals, you know, they're often hurrying around, getting to work, bored with their commutes.
sentences.zh: 但如果我们看看当地人，你知道的，他们经常行色匆匆地赶去上班，对通勤感到厌倦。

sentences.en: And they're seeing the same city that you're seeing, but, of course, your experience of it is completely different.
sentences.zh: 他们看到的城市和你看到的是一样的，但当然，你的体验完全不同。

sentences.en: And similarly, when you're in your home city and you see tourists, you know, the tourists are standing around taking pictures of buildings that you walk by every day,
sentences.zh: 同样的，当你身处自己的城市看到游客时，你知道的，游客们站在那里，拍着你每天走过、

sentences.en: and you've never stopped to look at the building, let alone take a picture of it.
sentences.zh: 却从未驻足欣赏过、更别说拍照的建筑物。

sentences.en: And in some ways, that's speaking to exactly the idea that you're talking about, Cassie.
sentences.zh: 从某种程度上说，这正切合了你刚才谈到的观点，卡西。

sentences.en: There's something about being a tourist in our own lives that in some ways opens us up and makes us pay attention and be mindful of what's happening around us.
sentences.zh: 在自己的生活中当一次游客，这种体验在某种程度上能让我们敞开心扉，让我们关注并留心周围发生的事情。

sentences.en: Absolutely.
sentences.zh: 完全正确。

sentences.en: And the thing that we're subject to in the routine of our lives is that we get used to it.
sentences.zh: 而我们在日常生活常规中容易遇到的问题是，我们习以为常了。

sentences.en: Our tendency to hedonically adapt, it's called hedonic adaptation, that is, after repeated exposure, we stop noticing it as much.
sentences.zh: 我们习惯于享乐适应，这被称为享乐适应，也就是说，在反复接触后，我们不再那么注意到它了。

sentences.en: And this is good that we adopt when bad things happen because it makes us resilient, but it's not so good in the face of, you know,
sentences.zh: 当我们遭遇不顺时，这种适应能力是件好事，因为它能让我们变得坚韧，但在面对，你知道的，

sentences.en: joys in our life because we don't notice them as much.
sentences.zh: 生活中的快乐时，它就没那么好了，因为我们不再那么注意到它们了。

sentences.en: You know, if you think about the first time your partner said, I love you, you know, your heart is bursting with happiness.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，如果你回想一下你的伴侣第一次对你说“我爱你”的时候，你知道的，你的内心充满了幸福感。

sentences.en: And then 10 years on in a marriage, I love you, it has been shortened to love you as a way to sort of say goodbye in the morning, and you don't even hear the words.
sentences.zh: 而在结婚十年后，“我爱你”被简化成了“爱呀”，作为早晨道别的一种方式，你甚至都听不到那些话了。

sentences.en: So there is something that when things happen every day, they feel every day, and we don't notice,
sentences.zh: 因此，当事情每天都在发生时，它们就会变得日常化，而我们便会忽视，

sentences.en: and we're missing out on the potential joy from those pleasures that are right there in our daily experience.
sentences.zh: 我们也错失了那些就存在于我们日常生活体验中的快乐所带来的潜在喜悦。

sentences.en: Cassie started to ask, are there other techniques to get people to change their relationship to time?
sentences.zh: 卡西开始发问：还有其他什么技术能让人改变与时间的关系吗？

sentences.en: In one study, she gave volunteers a set of tasks and asked some of them to think about time and some of them to think about money.
sentences.zh: 在一项研究中，她给志愿者布置了一组任务，并要求其中一部分人思考时间，另一部分人思考金钱。

sentences.en: What I found was that those who were led to think about time compared to a control condition and a money condition actually planned to engage in activities that were happier activities.
sentences.zh: 我发现，与对照组和金钱组相比，被引导去思考时间的人实际上更有计划去从事能带来更多快乐的活动。

sentences.en: So involving social connection or those activities that made them feel fulfillment.
sentences.zh: 也就是包含社交连接，或是那些能让他们感到满足的活动。

sentences.en: In other words, one way to change the way you spend your time is to simply ask yourself how you are spending your time.
sentences.zh: 换句话说，改变你度过时间的方式的一个方法，就是简单地问问自己你是如何度过时间的。

sentences.en: Cassie has found that once people are put into a state of mind where they are thinking about time, their behavior changes too.
sentences.zh: 卡西发现，一旦人们进入思考时间的思维状态，他们的行为也会随之改变。

sentences.en: In my work, I didn't just want to see how people plan to spend their time.
sentences.zh: 在我的研究中，我不只想看看人们计划如何度过时间。

sentences.en: I also wanted to see how thinking about time versus money would influence people's actual behavior.
sentences.zh: 我还想看看思考时间与金钱会如何影响人们的实际行为。

sentences.en: So I went to a coffee shop as a place where, you know, people are socially connecting and spending time with others,
sentences.zh: 因此，我去了咖啡馆，因为那里是一个，你知道的，人们进行社交连接和与他人共度时光的地方，

sentences.en: which is an activity that's associated with greater happiness.
sentences.zh: 而这是一个与更高的幸福感息息相关的活动。

sentences.en: And people also, you know, are on their laptops working.
sentences.zh: 人们也，你知道的，在笔记本电脑前工作。

sentences.en: On the way into the cafe, I asked them to complete a survey, which surreptitiously exposed them to time-related words or money-related words.
sentences.zh: 在进入咖啡馆的路上，我请他们完成一份调查问卷，该问卷在不知不觉中让他们接触到了与时间相关的词汇或与金钱相关的词汇。

sentences.en: And then, unbeknownst to the participants, we watched how they spent their time in the cafe.
sentences.zh: 然后，在参与者不知情的情况下，我们观察了他们在咖啡馆里是如何度过时间的。

sentences.en: And what we found was that those who were led to think about time spent a greater proportion of their time at the cafe connecting with others.
sentences.zh: 我们发现，那些被引导去思考时间的人在咖啡馆里花更多的时间与他人连接。

sentences.en: So chatting with others in line, talking to others in the space versus those who were actually led to think about money spent a greater proportion of their time working.
sentences.zh: 也就是说，与那些被引导去思考金钱的人相比，他们花更多的时间在排队时与他人闲聊、在空间里与他人交谈，而后者花更多的时间在工作上。

sentences.en: And so I think what this research shows is that thinking about our time, being more thoughtful and intentional about this resource that is our life, right?
sentences.zh: 所以我认为这项研究表明，思考我们的时间，对我们作为生命资源的这一点更加深思熟虑和有意识，对吧？

sentences.en: How we spend our minutes, add up to our hours, our years, our decades in our life overall.
sentences.zh: 我们如何度过每一个分钟，汇聚成了我们生命中的小时、年份、甚至数十年。

sentences.en: And when we're thinking about this resource, it makes us spend more deliberately in ways that are aligned with our values, in ways that make us feel happier.
sentences.zh: 当我们思考这种资源时，它会促使我们更深思熟虑地去消费，去采取那些符合我们价值观、让我们感到更快乐的方式。

sentences.en: I understand that you've sometimes had volunteers do a rather unusual exercise, which is to write their own eulogies.
sentences.zh: 我听说你有时会让志愿者做一个相当不寻常的练习，那就是写他们自己的悼词。

sentences.en: Why would you ask them to do this, Cassie?
sentences.zh: 你为什么要让他们这么做呢，卡西？

sentences.en: Yeah, what writing your eulogy does is it leads you to think, take that broader perspective of your time, thinking about your life as a whole.
sentences.zh: 是的，写悼词所能做到的，就是引导你去思考，从更广阔的视角来看待你的时间，把你的生活作为一个整体来思考。

sentences.en: So it is how at the end of your life do you want to be remembered?
sentences.zh: 也就是在你的生命终结时，你希望人们如何记住你？

sentences.en: What legacy do you want to leave?
sentences.zh: 你想留下什么样的传承？

sentences.en: And by articulating that, writing out a eulogy that you would hope that will be presented about you, what it clarifies is,
sentences.zh: 通过表达这一点，写下一份你希望别人在悼词中对你的评价，这所能阐明的是，

sentences.en: is what are those aspects of you that are really important?
sentences.zh: 你身上那些真正重要的方面是什么？

sentences.en: What are those words that you hope people use to describe you?
sentences.zh: 你希望人们用什么词来形容你？

sentences.en: What are your values?
sentences.zh: 你的价值观是什么？

sentences.en: And by thinking about that, what life do you want to live?
sentences.zh: 通过思考这些，你想过什么样的生活？

sentences.en: That can inform how you spend your hours today.
sentences.zh: 这可以为你是如何度过今天的每一个小时提供指导。

sentences.en: Another technique along the same lines is called the times left exercise.
sentences.zh: 另一个类似的技巧被称为“剩余时间”练习。

sentences.en: So if you reflect back on your past week and identify what was a moment of joy, oftentimes it's a very ordinary experience.
sentences.zh: 所以，如果你回顾过去的一周，找出快乐的时刻是什么，通常这都是非常平凡的体验。

sentences.en: And so what I encourage people to do is count how many times have you done that in your life so far?
sentences.zh: 所以我鼓励人们做的是，数一数到目前为止你在生活中已经做过多少次这样的事情？

sentences.en: And then to count how many times do you have left to do it in your life?
sentences.zh: 然后数一数，在你的余生中，你还有多少次机会去做这件事？

sentences.en: An example here is I had, I have my students do this.
sentences.zh: 这里有个例子，我让我的学生们做过这个。

sentences.en: And one of my students who is in her late 20s getting her MBA, counted her dinners with her parents.
sentences.zh: 我有一个二十多岁正在读MBA的学生，她计算了她和父母一起吃晚餐的次数。

sentences.en: And what she calculated, thinking about, you know, from her childhood, other than the study, you know, summer that she was studying abroad in high school.
sentences.zh: 她计算的结果是，考虑到，你知道的，从她的童年开始，除了那次她在高中时出国交流学习的研究夏天以外。

sentences.en: And then counting once she went off to college, visits home, and then when she was living in on the other side of the country for work, when her parents would come out to visit.
sentences.zh: 然后计算她上大学之后回家的探亲次数，接着是她为了工作住在国家另一端时父母过去看望的次数。

sentences.en: And then she moved back to California to actually be closer to her parents.
sentences.zh: 然后她搬回了加利福尼亚，为了能离父母更近一些。

sentences.en: And they had Sunday night dinners.
sentences.zh: 他们一起吃周日晚晚餐。

sentences.en: And she counted all of those up and realized that she had had about 6,800 dinners with her parents thus far in her life.
sentences.zh: 她把这些全部加起来，意识到在迄今为止的人生中，她大约和父母吃过6800次晚餐。

sentences.en: And then in calculating how many dinners does she likely have left, she counted that she had about 575 dinners left.
sentences.zh: 然后在计算她可能还剩下多少次晚餐时，她算出自己大概还剩下575次晚餐。

sentences.en: That is, she had only 8% of her dinners with her parents left.
sentences.zh: 也就是说，她和父母一起吃晚餐的机会只剩下8%了。

sentences.en: And that's impactful because what it does is it leads her to, A, make the time.
sentences.zh: 这很有冲击力，因为它的作用是促使她：A，腾出时间。

sentences.en: No matter how busy she feels, that she, with that recognition, she is going to show up for the Sunday night dinner.
sentences.zh: 无论她觉得多么忙碌，带着这种认知，她都会出席周日晚上的晚餐。

sentences.en: But even beyond that, at the dinners, it changes how she engages in that time.
sentences.zh: 但不仅如此，在晚餐上，它改变了她在那段时间里的投入方式。

sentences.en: You know, like her mom's, what she used to view as nagging comments.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，比如她妈妈的、她以前视为唠叨的那些评论。

sentences.en: She would just let roll off her shoulders.
sentences.zh: 她现在会选择直接一笑置之。

sentences.en: And instead, she, you know, redirected the conversation to learn about her parents, recognizing that their time together is limited and, more consequently, is really precious.
sentences.zh: 相反，她，你知道的，重新引导了谈话来了解她的父母，因为她认识到他们在一起的时间是有限的，更重要的是，它是如此珍贵。

sentences.en: And so wanting to make the most of it.
sentences.zh: 因此她想要充分利用这段时间。

sentences.en: You know, it's so interesting that I think once something is in the past, it's easy to recognize how precious it was.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，这真是有趣，我认为一旦事情成为过去，就很容易认识到它是多么珍贵。

sentences.en: I mean, when you think about the walks you had with your son when he was going to preschool across the UCLA campus when you were too busy to smell the roses,
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，当你回想当年你儿子上学前班时，你陪他在UCLA校园里散步的情景，那时你总是太忙而无暇驻足闻闻花香，

sentences.en: you can look back on that now and realize it was really precious.
sentences.zh: 你现在回过头来看，就会意识到那真的很珍贵。

sentences.en: But at the time, you were like, how do I get through this walk really quickly so I can drop him off to get to work?
sentences.zh: 但在当时，你的想法是：我怎么才能快点走完这段路，好把他放下然后去上班呢？

sentences.en: There's a real irony there, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 这里面有着真正的讽刺意味，不是吗？

sentences.en: Which is when we look back, we can actually see how precious things are.
sentences.zh: 那就是当我们回首往事时，我们确实能看出事物有多么珍贵。

sentences.en: But when we look in the present, we often fail to notice that things, in fact, are precious and are finite.
sentences.zh: 但当我们审视现在时，我们常常没有注意到，事物其实是珍贵且有限的。

sentences.en: Yeah, and that's why it's so important to recognize their preciousness before we've passed them by, so that we don't end up feeling regret.
sentences.zh: 是的，这就是为什么在它们从我们身边溜走之前认识到它们的珍贵是如此重要，这样我们才不会最终感到遗憾。

sentences.en: Cassie has also found another powerful way to help people achieve a healthier relationship with time.
sentences.zh: 卡西还发现了另一种强有力的方法，可以帮助人们与时间建立更健康的联系。

sentences.en: Seek out moments of transcendence.
sentences.zh: 去寻找超越自我的时刻。

sentences.en: Awe is this state where your perspective expands well beyond yourself.
sentences.zh: 敬畏感是一种能让你的视野远远超越自身的精神状态。

sentences.en: When we feel our time is scarce, we behave in very limiting ways that we pull into ourselves, that we don't think about,
sentences.zh: 当我们觉得时间紧缺时，我们的行为会变得非常局限，我们会自我收缩，我们不会去考虑，

sentences.en: we don't have confidence that we can complete all that we sort of want to and ideally would like to do.
sentences.zh: 我们也没有信心能够完成我们想要以及理想中想要做的所有事情。

sentences.en: Whereas by shifting our perspective, expanding our perspective, then it also expands our sense of how much time that we have.
sentences.zh: 然而，通过转变我们的视角、拓宽我们的视野，它同时也扩展了我们对所拥有时间的感知。

sentences.en: Not all of us, of course, can hang out of the Grand Canyon with mouths agape.
sentences.zh: 当然，我们并不是所有人都能大张着嘴站在大峡谷边。

sentences.en: Most of us are not astronauts who get to see the Earth from outer space.
sentences.zh: 我们大多数人也不是能够从外太空俯瞰地球的宇航员。

sentences.en: But Cassie argues that there is a simple way for each of us to get out of our own head.
sentences.zh: 但卡西认为，我们每个人都有一个简单的方法来跳出自己的思维局限。

sentences.en: Exercise is this activity that unfortunately we often don't do when we feel that we don't have a lot of time.
sentences.zh: 运动就是这样一项活动，不幸的是，当我们觉得时间不够时，我们往往不会去做。

sentences.en: I often ask people to complete the sentence, I don't have time to blank.
sentences.zh: 我经常请人们完成这样一句话：我没有时间去空缺处填空。

sentences.en: And exercise is often one of those things that people don't feel they have time to do.
sentences.zh: 而运动往往就是人们觉得没有时间去做的那些事情之一。

sentences.en: And that is not good because exercise, research has shown that exercise is wonderful.
sentences.zh: 这可不好，因为运动，研究已经表明运动太棒了。

sentences.en: It increases our cognitive functioning.
sentences.zh: 它能提高我们的认知功能。

sentences.en: It increases our self-esteem.
sentences.zh: 它能提升我们的自尊心。

sentences.en: So making us feel like we can accomplish what we set out to do.
sentences.zh: 从而让我们觉得自己能够完成我们着手去做的事情。

sentences.en: And it's a mood booster.
sentences.zh: 而且它是一种情绪助推器。

sentences.en: It makes us feel happier in our subsequent activities.
sentences.zh: 它能让我们在接下来的活动中感到更快乐。

sentences.en: How we experience the limiting nature of time when we feel that time is scarce.
sentences.zh: 当我们觉得时间稀缺时，我们是如何体验到时间的局限性的。

sentences.en: We don't feel like we have enough time to complete what we set out to do.
sentences.zh: 我们觉得没有足够的时间来完成我们着手去做的事情。

sentences.en: But by exercising, through increasing our sense of self-efficacy, it actually expands our sense of what we can complete within our given time.
sentences.zh: 但通过运动，通过增强我们的自我效能感，它实际上扩大了我们在给定时间内能够完成的事情的感知。

sentences.en: And I am absolutely subject to this.
sentences.zh: 而我绝对也深受其害。

sentences.en: When I don't feel like I have time, my early morning run is the thing that I sacrifice because I'm like, oh, I need to get ready for the day.
sentences.zh: 当我感觉没有时间时，我清晨的跑步就是我牺牲掉的事情，因为我想：哦，我需要为这一天做准备。

sentences.en: I need to catch up on email.
sentences.zh: 我需要回复积压的电子邮件。

sentences.en: But in those moments or at those times where I do make the time, out on that run, as the sun is rising and I am in flow, I all of a sudden don't feel constrained.
sentences.zh: 但在那些我确实挤出时间的时刻或时间里，在那次跑步中，当太阳升起而我处于心流状态时，我突然不再感到受束缚了。

sentences.en: In fact, I sort of approach the day.
sentences.zh: 事实上，我仿佛迎向了这一天。

sentences.en: I come back, you know, running up the steps, ready for the day, nicer to those around us.
sentences.zh: 我回来了，你知道的，跑上台阶，为新的一天做好准备，对身边的人也更友善了。

sentences.en: We talked about how being time poor makes us stingier with our time with respect to others.
sentences.zh: 我们讨论过，时间贫困如何让我们在对待他人时，在时间上变得更加吝啬。

sentences.en: And so it is a very expanding activity.
sentences.zh: 所以它是一个能让人极大开阔心胸的活动。

sentences.en: Well, so many of these ideas really speak to the notion that when we are in some ways thinking expansively about our time, as opposed to in this very, you know, I'm stressed out,
sentences.zh: 嗯，其中许多观点确实印证了这样一个概念：当我们以某种开阔的方式思考我们的时间，而不是处于这种非常，你知道的，“我很压力山大、

sentences.en: I'm burned out, I don't have time.
sentences.zh: 我已经筋疲力尽、我没有时间”的状态中。

sentences.en: When we don't have this, you know, the walls are closing in mentality, in some ways almost it opens up the possibilities of what we can do with our time.
sentences.zh: 当我们没有这种，你知道的，四面楚歌的心态时，在某种程度上，它几乎为我们用时间能做的事情开启了无限可能。

sentences.en: Does it seem that way to you, Cassie?
sentences.zh: 你觉得是这样吗，卡西？

sentences.en: Yes, it opens up the possibilities of what we can do with our time.
sentences.zh: 是的，它开启了我们用时间所能做的事情的种种可能。

sentences.en: It also makes us think about our time from a broader perspective, from a bird's eye view, where we're thinking more about our years and less hour by hour.
sentences.zh: 它还促使我们从更广泛的视角、从鸟瞰的角度来思考我们的时间，让我们更多地思考我们的年份，而不是一小时一小时地计较。

sentences.en: And with that broader perspective, then it's more of these questions of what do I value in life?
sentences.zh: 有了这个更广阔的视角，接下来就会引发更多关于“我在生活中看重什么？”的问题。

sentences.en: And that influences how we, where we spend our time, spending more on things that are important rather than just urgent.
sentences.zh: 这会影响我们如何以及在哪里花费时间，让我们把更多时间花在那些重要的事情上，而不是仅仅是紧急的事情上。

sentences.en: In some ways, Cassie, so much of this work has been about the idea that we miss the forest for the trees when it comes to time.
sentences.zh: 从某种意义上说，卡西，这其中的许多工作都围绕着这样一个理念：在时间这件事情上，我们往往只见树木，不见森林。

sentences.en: And in many ways, when we step back and look at the big picture of time, it changes our relationship to time in really profound ways.
sentences.zh: 在许多情况下，当我们退一步审视时间的宏大全景时，它会以非常深刻的方式改变我们与时间的关系。

sentences.en: I'm wondering whether you've taken this inside to heart yourself.
sentences.zh: 我很想知道你是否把这个深刻见解铭记于心了？

sentences.en: How has this changed the way you lead your own life?
sentences.zh: 这如何改变了你领导自己生活的方式？

sentences.en: I absolutely, it influences both how I spend my time spending on activities that are,
sentences.zh: 我绝对这样做了，它既影响了我如何度过时间——把时间花在那些，

sentences.en: no matter how busy I feel, on those activities that are truly important to me, that connect me with the people I love,
sentences.zh: 无论我感觉多么忙碌，都花在对我真正重要、能将我和我爱的人连接起来的活动上，

sentences.en: that allow me to engage with work that does feel purposeful.
sentences.zh: 这些活动让我能够投入到确实有目标感的工作中。

sentences.en: But I would say even more than the types of activities that I engage with, it's really how I approach that time.
sentences.zh: 但我要说，比起我所从事的活动类型，它更深刻地影响了我对待这些时间的方式。

sentences.en: And it's not even so much about how much time you spend, it's really how engaged, how not distracted one is, or I am, so that I'm not missing out.
sentences.zh: 甚至不在于你花了多少时间，而在于你有多投入、有多专注，或者说我有多专注，这样我就不会错过任何东西。

sentences.en: An example that is so precious to me is my morning coffee dates with my daughter.
sentences.zh: 对我来说非常珍贵的一个例子是我和女儿的晨间咖啡约会。

sentences.en: Once a week, my daughter Lita and I go to a coffee shop, and this started actually as a very routine, functional activity,
sentences.zh: 每周一次，我和女儿莉塔会去一家咖啡馆，这最初其实是一个非常例行公事的、功能性的活动，

sentences.en: where after dropping off her big brother's carpool, on the way into dropping her at her preschool, which is next to my office,
sentences.zh: 当时是在拼车送她哥哥去完学校后，在顺路送她去我办公室隔壁的学前班的路上，

sentences.en: we would stop for coffee because I needed caffeine, and she was just tagging along.
sentences.zh: 我们会顺便买杯咖啡，因为我需要咖啡因，而她只是顺便跟着。

sentences.en: But what was routine, we turned it into this special tradition, and during that half hour, we would sit and delight in each other's company.
sentences.zh: 但我们把原本例行公事的事情变成了一个特别的传统，在那半小时里，我们会坐在一起享受彼此的陪伴。

sentences.en: I would drink my coffee, she would drink her hot chocolate, we would munch on croissants, and we would just be together.
sentences.zh: 我会喝我的咖啡，她会喝她的热巧克力，我们会吃着可颂面包，我们只是静静地待在一起。

sentences.en: And it was 30 minutes in the week, but that 30 minutes when you asked me how happy I am in life,
sentences.zh: 那是一周里的30分钟，但当你问我我对生活有多幸福时，

sentences.en: I am absolutely happy, because that 30 minutes is time that I look forward to, that we look forward to.
sentences.zh: 我绝对是幸福的，因为那30分钟是我翘首以盼、是我们共同期待的时光。

sentences.en: So we anticipate while spending it, we're happy.
sentences.zh: 所以我们在度过它时充满期待，在经历时感到快乐。

sentences.en: And reflecting back, we remember it as this, and we think about it as this source of true connection.
sentences.zh: 而回首往事时，我们把它记作、并将其视为真正连接的源泉。

sentences.en: And I feel I have a wonderful relationship with my daughter, that from this 30 minutes, it colors my week,
sentences.zh: 我觉得我和女儿有着美妙的关系，正是这30分钟，给我的整个星期涂上了色彩，

sentences.en: and really the joy that I feel in my life overall.
sentences.zh: 也真正赋予了我对整个生活的快乐感受。

sentences.en: Cassie Holmes is a social psychologist at UCLA.
sentences.zh: 卡西·霍姆斯是加州大学洛杉矶分校的社会心理学家。

sentences.en: She's the author of Happier Hour, How to Beat Distraction, Expand Your Time, and Focus on What Matters MoSt.
sentences.zh: 她著有《更快乐的小时：如何战胜分心、拓展时间并专注于最重要的事情》。

sentences.en: Cassie, thank you so much for joining me today on Hidden Brain.
sentences.zh: 卡西，非常感谢你今天做客我们的《隐藏的大脑》。谢谢。

sentences.en: Thank you.
sentences.zh: 谢谢你。

sentences.zh: 因此，《Hidden Brain》对健康也有益处。

sentences.zh: 谢谢你，彼得，感谢你将《Hidden Brain》作为你健身日常的一部分，也感谢你对本节目的支持。

sentences.zh: 我是香卡·韦丹塔姆。

sentences.zh: 再见。
